summary: Draft updated at submission.json (validated read-only: valid, no diagnostics). This update records the retained execution for the Node API question: investigation b8fa9bc20e164089beff30308ce68220-question-0 now has an interpretation for its own experiment b8fa9bc20e164089beff30308ce68220-experiment with conclusion violated, citing receipt d5f37430774c4bbd9d64967e3f82290d (completed, exit 0, tests_passed, no parsing errors, 4 parsed events) at decisive parsed indices 0, 1, 2 and 3. Predicate as declared: after a node applied a configuration that removes it, a proposal through the Node API is reported as not admissible instead of blocking until the caller's deadline. It is violated at index 3, correlated to its own admission at index 2 - the node was confirmed absent from voters [1,2], and the same Node.Propose call blocked for 201 ms against a 200 ms timeout and returned only 'context deadline exceeded', carrying no statement about membership - while the member control holds at index 1 (no error, 0 ms, still in the configuration), which excludes a harness, transport or timeout artifact. The mechanism is sourced: node.run disables the proposal channel when the node applies its own removal (node.go:405-433, with the source's own note that the re-enable-on-leadership-change handling 'isn't very sound and likely has bugs'), and Propose's wait path can only complete on that channel, the caller's context or the node's done channel (node.go:513-537), so the drop the raft layer produces in the comparable removed-leader case (raft.go:1290-1295) never appears here. A Fact entry records the instance with its receipt and operands, and the question is marked explained with the sourced Behaviour entry as its premise. Counterevidence is explicit that the block is deliberate in the source, that a caller-supplied deadline bounds the call (as observed), and that only a non-expiring context would hang indefinitely - a stronger case recorded as unmeasured rather than observed; the remaining limitations cover single-run scope, follower-removal only, and embedding-service policies outside the captured package. No new experiment is requested this turn.
